newsitem.title: Netherlands: U.N. Court elects American judge as president.
newsitem.headline: U.N. Court elects American judge as president.

text.p: The International Court of Justice has elected Judge Stephen Schwebel of the United States as its new president for a three-year term, the court's registry said on Thursday.
He replaces Mohammed Bedjaoui of Algeria as president of the court, which is the main judicial organ of the United Nations and settles disputes between states according to international law.
Schwebel, born in New York City on March 10, 1929, has been a member of the court since January 1981.
Admitted to the bar of New York state in 1955, he was later professor of international law at John Hopkins University, Washington D.C., and a State Department legal adviser.
The court is made up of 15 judges elected for terms of nine years by the U.N. Security Council and the General Assembly.
Five judges are elected every three years, after which all 15 judges elect a new president for the next three years.
Judge Christopher Weeramantry of Sri Lanka was elected vice-president of the court.
